english.notes:
(i) If no intent to avoid the fare can be proved, consider subsection 5(1), of the Regulation of Railways Act 1889 - fail to show ticket, pay fare, give name/address.
(ii) Payment of the fare means payment of the proper fare, so an offence can be committed by travelling first class on a standard class ticket. (Gillingham v Walker 1881 44 LT 715).
(iii) A demand for payment of the excess fare does not bar criminal proceedings. (Noble v Killick 1891 LJMC 61).
(iv) See also offence wording H1588.
